raw_response:
I'm 73 this year, and I've been working this land for 50 years. My wife and I are the only ones left at home — our children went to Shijiazhuang to work in the factories. We have 2.6 mu, all in cotton. I thought about trying wheat-maize double cropping like some younger folks, but at my age I can't handle that rush. Cotton is slower, and I understand it.

I don't have much cash lying around, so every yuan matters. I'll plant around April 20th, when the soil warms up. I buy improved seeds from the shop in town — last year I tried saving my own seeds, but the seedlings came up weak and patchy. Seed costs about 35 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll spread base fertilizer when I plant: some compound fertilizer and urea mixed together. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I'll add more urea. I can't afford too much — maybe about 11 kg of nitrogen per mu total. My neighbor Old Wang cut back on fertilizer last year to save money, and his cotton turned yellow and stunted. I won't make that mistake.

I'll irrigate twice: once after planting if the rain doesn't come, and again when the bolls are setting. Pumping water from the well costs electricity, so I don't waste it. For pests, I'll spray herbicide once after planting, and insecticide two or three times when I see bollworms or aphids. My wife and I do all the work ourselves. Hiring labor now costs over 100 yuan a day, which I can't pay. Picking takes the longest — we go through the field three or four times from September to October. It's hard on these old bones, but we manage. If the weather is decent, I expect about 250 kg per mu. Not as good as the big farms, but enough for us.
